memos.scout:
The honest case for buying XP now is weak. The strongest point is that it is alive, classified ORGANIC, with no airdrop dump seen, and that over the last 15 minutes it attracted 1,495 buyers and 857 SOL of buy volume (about $211k), so real trading interest exists and the pool holds 176 SOL of depth, which keeps round-trip impact manageable for a $20 ticket.

But the rest of the brief argues against entry. Buy-side demand is already fading: net flow over 15 minutes is -23.65 SOL, sellers (657) are rising alongside buyers, and the coin is down 34.6% over that window and 43% from its 30-minute high. The early curve is concentrated: the first 2 minutes show a launch bot, a top-5 buyer share of 47.6%, and a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.56, which means early participants have been exiting. Bundle share is 1.0 and top-3 share is 1.0, suggesting coordinated early accumulation rather than broad organic demand.

I see no evidence in the brief that demand will hold 30-60 minutes out. My recommendation is to skip. A bounce is possible, but nothing here distinguishes it from the base-rate loss of buying a declining, concentrated coin.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss is insider distribution after a bundled launch. The curve data shows bundle_share at 1.0, top3_share at 1.0, and only 3 buyers on the curve, so nearly all early supply sat with a handful of coordinated wallets. The first two minutes after graduation show 316 SOL of buys against a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.56 and a launch bot present, which suggests the bundled wallets were already unwinding into retail demand. Last 15 minutes: net flow is -23.65 SOL, sellers (657) outnumber the flow's support, and the coin is down 43% from its 30-minute high. Pool depth of 176 SOL is thin for the $211k of volume, so a $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% costs plus slippage, and any further dip leaves little room for a bounce. Skip.
